parole.significato: The fibre obtained from the husk of a coconut, used chiefly in making rope, matting and as a peat substitute.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil கயிறு (kayiṟu), Malayalam കയർ (kayaṟ).

parole.significato: A type of thick rice porridge or soup, sometimes prepared with vegetables and/or meat.
parole.testo: From Tamil கஞ்சி (kañci) or another Dravidian language such as Malayalam കഞ്ഞി (kaññi) (ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *kañci), possibly via Portuguese canje.

parole.significato: A monumental tower, usually ornate, at the entrance of a temple, especially in Southern India.
parole.testo: From Tamil கோபுரம் (kōpuram), Malayalam ഗോപുരം (gōpuraṁ), from Sanskrit गोपुर (gó-pura).
Probably from Tamil கிரந்தம் (kirantam), Malayalam ഗ്രന്ഥം (granthaṁ), or similar, ultimately from Sanskrit ग्रन्थ (grantha). Grantha script was used for writing Sanskrit in South India.

parole.significato: A layered flatbread of parts of South Asia, made with maida flour.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil பரோட்டா (parōṭṭā) and/or Malayalam പൊറോട്ട (poṟōṭṭa), in turn borrowed from Marathi परोठा (paroṭhā). Doublet of paratha.

parole.significato: Any of several East Indian trees of the genus Calophyllum, yielding a light, hard wood used for masts, spars, etc.
parole.testo: Compare Tamil புன்னை (puṉṉai), Malayalam പുന്ന (punna), names for Calophyllum inophyllum. Doublet of punnai.
